question.problem: What is $\dfrac {\left(\dfrac 1 4\right)} {\left(-\dfrac 3 7\right)}$ expressed as a single fraction?
question.worked_solution:
First, remember that a fraction represents a division.  So, a fraction of fractions is a division of two fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(\frac{1}{4})}{(-\frac{3}{7})} & =\frac{1}{4}÷(-\frac{3}{7})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that dividing by $-\dfrac{3}{7}$ is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal $-\dfrac{7}{3}.$ We can use this fact to simplify the fraction above:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}÷(-\frac{3}{7}) & = \\ \frac{1}{4}\times (-\frac{7}{3}) & = \\ -\frac{1\times 7}{4\times 3} & = \\ -\frac{7}{12} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(\frac{1}{4})}{(-\frac{3}{7})} & =-\frac{7}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the fact that a positive number times a negative number gives a negative number.
